data.narrative:
Alpha School, founded by MacKenzie Price and Brian Holtz, is a Series A artificial intelligence and software company. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of four same-sector, same- or adjacent-stage companies: Reflection AI ($25.0B Series A), Together AI ($8.3B Series A), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B Series B), and Black Forest Labs ($3.2B Series B). The broader AI & Software comp universe includes one public company (Palantir) and eight private firms.

The peer-median method, the single applicable triangulation approach given current data availability, yields an implied valuation of $7.0B. This median reflects the central tendency across the four-company sample, which ranges from $3.2B to $25.0B. The wide dispersion—a 7.8x spread between minimum and maximum—reflects material variation in stage, capitalization, and likely investor appetite within the frontier AI subsector at Series A and Series B.

The triangulated valuation range of $5.9B to $8.0B (median $7.0B) is supported by peer-median analysis alone. Key uncertainties include the limited comp set size, the heterogeneity introduced by inclusion of Series B peers alongside Series A, and the absence of revenue, growth rate, or capital efficiency metrics to differentiate Alpha School's profile within this range. Revenue multiples or unit economics data would strengthen conviction in placement within the $5.9B–$8.0B band.
